desc_src: The Vollis Simpson Whirliigig Park on Goldsboro Street S. at Douglas Street S. in Wilson, North Carolina, opened on November 2, 2017 to document, conserve, and display the large whirlgigs from Simpson's property in Lucama, North Carolina. Wilson held its first annual Wilson Whirligig Festival in 2004. It was renamed in 2016 to the North Carolina Whirligig Festival, and is usually held the first full weekend of November. The North Carolina legislature named the whirligig the state's official folk art in June 2013.

Home to the 26th President, gentleman farmer Teddy Roodevelt, Sagamore Hill was a working farm in Oyster Bay, NY. Historical Marker for the Sagamore Hill National Historic Site is along Sagamore Hill Road in Cove Neck, New York, which is in the Town of Oyster Bay. Windvanes on windpump.

Ornamental wrought-iron weather vane located at the top of the roof of the San Telmo Modernist Kiosk in Las Palmas de Gran Canaria. The building was designed by architect Rafael Massanet y Faus in 1923. This artistic metalwork element crowns the structure and combines its function of indicating wind direction with a decorative purpose, forming part of the building's architectural ornamentation.
